title: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to take user account records and source code; vaults not accessed
date_note: 1Password's post of 25 November says it began investigating on 19 November; the page gives no earlier day for the intrusion itself, so the post's publication day is used.
geo_basis: no location stated in the sources read
summary: 1Password says it began investigating on 19 November after signs that an attacker had accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account. The company says the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of users (names, email addresses, identifiers, sign-in times) and some invitation and recovery email tokens, and copied source code from private repositories. 1Password says vault contents were never accessed and it found no evidence of account takeovers.
plain: 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's GitHub account and took some user account records, some email tokens and source code. It says customers' vault contents were never accessed.
exec: A password-manager vendor reports a breach of its source code and some user records; it says vaults were not accessed.
action: 1Password advises that no action is needed in your account, and to be cautious of unexpected emails, texts or calls about 1Password, invitations or account recovery.
impact: Account records for a subset of users and source code from private repositories, per 1Password.

validation.note: Primary: 1Password's own incident post. Dark Web Informer relays it and is not independent.

review.note: title, date, data accessed, vault statement, advice compared with 1Password post
